name: Anathoth
overview: Anathoth is a male figure identified as a non-Levite leader mentioned in the book of Nehemiah. He is named among the signatories of a sealed document in Nehemiah 10:19, indicating a position of responsibility during the post-exilic period. Although his tribal affiliation is not specified, his leadership role is noteworthy given his non-Levite status.
namesAndTitles: The name Anathoth is a proper name meaning the plural of Anath. This name is not indicated as being given by God but is referenced in Nehemiah 10:19. The meaning reflects a connection to the name Anath but does not provide further title or role information.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Anathoth is a descendant of Jacob, as noted in Nehemiah 10:19. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text for this individual.
scriptureSignificance: Anathoth's significance lies in his role as a leader who was part of the covenant renewal community described in Nehemiah 10. His inclusion on the sealed document highlights his commitment to the reforms and covenantal commitments undertaken by the returned exiles. His identification as a non-Levite leader underscores the broader involvement of various community members in the restoration efforts.
